instruction:
Extract all genuine structural headings in the document, at every level of its outline, including nested sections and subsections. Do not restrict selection to the highest-level headings.
A structural heading is a source occurrence that names, introduces, or divides a unit of document content at its actual location. It does not need to summarize that content in descriptive words.
A heading may span multiple source lines. A standalone structural label or number (such as "Chapter I") and a following descriptive title (such as "GENERAL PROVISIONS") may jointly form one heading. When the source context shows that they belong to the same heading, select every contributing source line and preserve its exact source alias. A standalone label may also function as a heading without a separate descriptive title.
Include genuine headings at all structural levels, including chapters, articles, sections, and lower-level subdivisions. Do not exclude an occurrence merely because it is subordinate to another heading.
Do not select numbered body paragraphs, table-of-contents references, cross-references, or other text merely because their wording, numbering, or appearance resembles a heading. Determine the structural function of each occurrence at its own location using its text, layout, and surrounding context.
When the available evidence cannot establish that function, request additional source evidence or report the occurrence as unresolved rather than guessing.
Formatting of a line (its style, font size, emphasis, alignment, numbering) is one kind of evidence, read together with the text, the place of the line in the outline and the lines around it. It does not by itself make a line a heading, and its absence does not by itself rule a line out.
A paragraph may contain both a structural heading and body text. Identify the heading by its structural function and determine its exact extent. Include only the text that belongs to the heading, even when body text continues in the same paragraph. Do not treat the entire paragraph as heading text merely because it begins with a heading.
Every fact the program gives about a line is a measurement to weigh, not a decision: no fact by itself makes a line a heading or rules it out.

lines.sourceText: Item 2: Operating Context. The GC welcomed the overview provided by the GC Members representing the Government of Ukraine indicating Ukraine’s budget and financing gap needs during 2025 and 2026 and the importance of the F.O.R.T.I.S. Ukraine FIF in ensuring adherence to the IMF Extended Fund Facility Arrangement on which the Ukrainian authorities and IMF staff have reached Staff Level Agreement on the Sixth Review; and for helping sustain the provision of humanitarian and social services.

Item 3: Strategic Directions. GC Members representing the Government of Ukraine indicated initial financing through the F.O.R.T.I.S Ukraine FIF is envisioned to be directed to direct budget support (DBS), but noted flexibility should be maintained to be able to shift financing as appropriate to recovery and reconstruction needs. Ukraine highlighted that funds from the F.O.R.T.I.S. Ukraine FIF are key in supporting Ukraine’s IMF program and cautioned that the downside financing needs scenario would require substantial DBS from the F.O.R.T.I.S. Ukraine

lines.sourceText: Item 4: Work Plan, Budget, and Fees. The GC agreed that the work plan and budget for the Secretariat and Trustee should be submitted by December 6, and that its approval can be made through Decision without a Meeting by December 13. The Secretariat committed to provide a note to the GC by December 6 describing the agreed approach to fees for the Secretariat, Trustee and the World Bank as Implementing Entity, and that its approval can be made through Decision without a Meeting by December 13.

Item 5: Communications Strategy. The GC agreed that the Secretariat will provide a plan and timeline for developing and making operational a web page by December 6, and that it can proceed with implementation of the plan through Decision without a Meeting. GC members noted that they may wish to exchange views on any early public communications.
Item 6: Appointment of the Chair. The GC selected the United States representative Brian McCauley as Chair of the F.O.R.T.I.S. FIF Ukraine for a period of one year.

1. Document Approval. Does the GC approve the (i) Governance Framework; (ii) Operations Manual; (iii) Standard Provisions of the Contribution Arrangement; (iv) Financial Procedures Agreement; and (iv) Funding Request Template.
2. Operating Context. The Government of Ukraine will take the floor to provide a general overview of the current operating context in Ukraine and Ukraine’s most pressing needs.

3. Strategic Directions. Does the GC agree that in setting strategic directions, this should include a discussion of Ukraine’s anticipated financing and recovery needs over the next three years, with a primary focus on the next 12 months, and how the FIF can best address those needs. The Government of Ukraine will submit a short Strategic Directions Note to the GC for comment and the Strategic Directions will be agreed by the GC prior to first disbursement.

4. Work Plan, Budget, and Fees. Does the GC agree that the work plan and budget for the Secretariat and Trustee should be submitted by December 6, and that its approval can be made through Decision without a Meeting by December 13? Does the GC agree that the Secretariat should provide a short note on the agreements reached around fees by December 6, and that its approval can be made through Decision without a Meeting by December 13

5. Communications Strategy. Does the GC agree that the Secretariat should provide a plan and timeline for developing a web page by December 6 and proceed with implementing the plan through Decision without a Meeting? Are there any other elements of an approach to communications that the GC wants to discuss/consider?
6. Appointment of the Chair. Does the GC approve the appointment of [Nominee] as the Chair for a period of one year?
